analysis:
Only scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py changed: a CI test harness for the Darkbloom route step and workflow pins. It is not part of the provider runtime, the coordinator/provider WebSocket contract (TB-002), attestation (TB-009/TB-011), or the prefix cache (T-041). No threat-model asset (A-001..A-020) is touched directly.

Test-side changes: build lanes now use requested() instead of built(); GPU lanes read a new cluster_gpu component; the Plane stub supports extra response headers (Retry-After); route tests exercise MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 6, bounds 1-9, invalid values must fail configuration); the subprocess timeout is raised to 160s; the hourly dispatch workflow and its hourly-failures job are removed.

The new `unlabel` job is tested to hold issues/pull-requests write on a literal ubuntu-24.04 runner, with no uses:, secrets. or checkout. All other jobs are asserted to lack those permissions. The watchdog test now evaluates the jq 'stranded' program to confirm partially-run Darkbloom attempts are not cancelled. The runner regex now also allows ubuntu-24.04 for unrouted workflows. These are tightening or neutral CI-hygiene assertions.

Not visible in the supplied evidence: the actual workflow files (darkbloom-route.yml, ci-dev.yml, ci-master.yml, provider-plan.yml, the watchdog). The security of the new `unlabel` write-permission job and the retry behavior depends on those files, which this unit does not show. If they are in the PR, the next pass should confirm that unlabel is gated on trusted events only (not fork-controlled pull_request_target) and that the retry cap and backoff cannot be abused. No concrete regression is identifiable from this file alone.
